title: A city was seconds away from destruction.
paragraphs: A city was seconds away from destruction.

The soldiers were already at the wall.
The battering rams were ready.
Dust filled the air.
Steel clanged against stone.
And inside that city… people were about to die for a sin they didn’t commit.

Not a queen.
Not a warrior.
Not a prophet.
Just a wise woman with the courage to speak.
This moment, recorded in 2 Samuel 20, is one of the most underrated rescue stories in the Bible.
After the rebellion of Absalom, another rebel rose up in Israel — a man named Sheba son of Bichri. Scripture calls him a “worthless man.” (2 Samuel 20:1)
He led a revolt against King David.
David sent his commander Joab to hunt him down.
The chase ended at a northern city called Abel Beth Maacah.
But Joab didn’t come to negotiate.
They began battering the wall to collapse it.

Children crying.
Families praying.
Men preparing to die.
All because one guilty man was hiding among them.

One person rebels…
And an entire community feels the shockwave.

One compromise.
One secret.
One act of pride.
And suddenly the walls of peace start shaking.
But in the middle of that chaos—

“Then a wise woman cried out from the city, ‘Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I can speak to him.’”
— 2 Samuel 20:16

She didn’t whisper.
She didn’t panic.
She didn’t stay silent.
She called the general of Israel’s army to the wall.
And when Joab came, she spoke words that cut through the madness.

“They used to say, ‘Let them ask counsel at Abel,’ and so they settled a matter. I am one who is peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up the heritage of the Lord?”
— 2 Samuel 20:18–19
She reminded Joab that this city wasn’t just a target.
God’s people should not be destroyed carelessly.

“Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy! That is not the case. A man named Sheba… has lifted up his hand against King David. Hand him over, and I will withdraw from the city.”
— 2 Samuel 20:20–21
Then the Bible gives one of the most fascinating lines in the story:

“Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom.”
— 2 Samuel 20:22
She convinced the city to deal with the rebellion inside the walls.
They threw his head over the wall.
All because one woman refused to stay silent.
A nameless woman saved an entire city with wisdom.
And there is a deeper spiritual picture here.
Sometimes we read this story and imagine ourselves as the city.
The compromise we think nobody knows.
Sin always brings destruction if it remains hidden.
It always puts the whole house in danger.
But here is where the Gospel explodes into the story.
Because Jesus did something Joab did not.
Instead of destroying the city to remove the sinner…
Christ allowed Himself to be destroyed to save the sinners.
The cross is where justice and mercy meet.
And it’s still saving people today.
So here’s the question this story asks every one of us:
What is hiding inside your walls?
The wise woman teaches us something powerful:
Peace doesn’t come from pretending evil isn’t there.
Peace comes when the rebellion is removed.
And the only place that can truly happen is at the cross of Jesus Christ.
God can use one courageous voice to save a household.
One moment of repentance to rescue a family.
One act of wisdom to protect a generation.
And sometimes the person God uses most…
Is someone history never even records the name of.
Someone out there is standing on a shaking wall right now.
Wisdom can still save the city.
